walk.title: Start-up: the composition root
walk.text: The one function that picks the concrete pieces and wires them. It checks the data files against the manifest, reads the spec, loads the weights through the store, and hands the network and the preprocessing to the predictor. Nothing further down imports its neighbours; each piece is given what it needs, here.

walk.title: The weights, trusted by digest
walk.text: The store recomputes the digest of the weights inside the file and refuses to load them if it differs from the one the evaluation recorded, so the network that answers is the one that was measured. Then it builds the network from the spec and pours the weights in.

walk.title: The network, built from its spec
walk.text: Nothing about the layers is written out by hand: the builder reads the spec shipped beside the code, block by block, and instantiates each one. The drawing on the network page is read from the same modules, so the two cannot disagree.

walk.title: A graph convolution
walk.text: Every {node.one} projects its vector with the same weights; then each {node.one} sums the projections of its neighbours, and its own with self loops, each scaled by the {edge.one} weight and by the degrees at both ends, and adds a bias. The coefficients are recomputed from the {edge.many}, so the explanation of a {node.one} names each neighbour's share.

walk.title: The non-linearity
walk.text: A function chosen by name from a table in this file bends each z. Without it the layers would multiply out into a single matrix — that single matrix is the effective linear reading the page gives for a unit, and the bend is why that reading is only an approximation.

walk.title: Dropout, off while answering
walk.text: While the network trains, dropout silences a random share of units so that none can lean on another. While it answers, it does nothing: the predictor puts the model in evaluation mode, so the same {row.one} always gets the same answer.

walk.title: The head: raw scores
walk.text: The last layer, with one output per score the task needs. These raw numbers, the logits, are what the stepper's output step shows before the link turns them into the answer.

walk.title: The forward pass
walk.text: The blocks applied in the order the spec lists them, each one reading what the one before it produced, or the nominal inputs or the graph it needs. Nothing else happens between the shaped numbers and the head's raw scores.

walk.title: Raw scores to the answer
walk.text: The link function of the task, applied once: it turns the head's raw scores into the answer, here and nowhere else, the same way the evaluation did.

walk.title: A raw {row.one}, shaped
walk.text: Before any of that, the recipe the data stage fitted on the training part is replayed with the parameters stored beside it — these are the x₁ … xₙ of the stepper's first step. This file was generated from the recipe, not written by hand, so it cannot drift from what the network was trained on.

walk.title: Answering a request
walk.text: The predictor assembles the shaped table into the batch the network reads, puts the network in evaluation mode, switches gradients off, and reads the head's output through the same readout the evaluation used.

walk.title: Where the explanation comes from
walk.text: Not a second model. The same forward pass runs with hooks, attached once when the service starts, that only read each stage's output; one backward pass from the explained output then gives, for each of them, how far it would move that output — its gradient. No weight is changed. The drawings weigh each edge by weight × activation × gradient; the families' bars are gradient × input.

walk.title: The HTTP route
walk.text: The request is checked against the input contract before any {row.one} reaches the predictor — a malformed {row.one} is refused with a report that names the column — and every answer carries the model's version, the digest of the weights that produced it.

"""The bundle's composition root: load() wires the adapters; the command line calls it."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

from pkg.model.network import build_model
from pkg.model.store import ModelRegistry
from pkg.serving.predict import Predictor


def bundle_root(bundle_dir=None) -> Path:
    return Path(bundle_dir or Path(__file__).parent)


def load(bundle_dir=None) -> Predictor:
    """Checks the files against the manifest, then wires the predictor."""
    root = bundle_root(bundle_dir)
    manifest = json.loads((root / "MANIFEST.json").read_text())

    spec = json.loads((root / "netspec.json").read_text())
    model = ModelRegistry().load(root / "weights.pt", spec=spec, build=build_model)
    return Predictor(model, manifest)


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    return 0 if load() else 1
